# STM32H743 FC + 80A 4-in-1 ESC (Job #13): Thermal, Switching, and Bi-Directional DShot Design Package

## 0. Scope and Architecture Caveats

**Who drives the gates.** The STM32H743 runs ArduPilot and only emits DShot600 frames. The 48 kHz bridge PWM is generated by four separate ESC MCUs running AM32 or BLHeli_32 (e.g., AT32F421 or STM32G071). The loss model below applies to the ESC power stage. The DMA model applies to the H743.

**Form factor reality check.** A 20×20 "nano" board cannot sustain 4×80 A. Section 3 shows the adiabatic burst limit is about 2–3 s even on a 30.5×30.5 stack. Treat "80A" as a per-channel burst rating with short duration and active prop-wash cooling.

**Parameters are assumptions.** Device values are representative of a 40 V, ~1 mΩ, PDFN 5×6 MOSFET class. Replace them with your selected part's datasheet values. The equations stay valid.

| Symbol | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| V_bus | 25.2 V | 6S, fully charged |
| I_ph | 80 A | burst phase current |
| f_sw | 48 kHz | |
| R_ds25 | 1.2 mΩ | max at Vgs = 10 V |
| α | 0.006 /K | R_ds(T_j) = R_ds25·[1+α(T_j−25)] |
| t_r + t_f | 40 ns | with a ~1.5 A gate driver |
| Q_rr | 40 nC | body diode |
| E_oss | from C_o(er) = 1.5 nF | |
| V_f | 0.8 V | body diode at 80 A |
| t_dead | 100 ns | per edge |
| Q_g | 50 nC | |
| V_gs | 10 V | |
| R_pcb | 0.5 mΩ | phase-path copper, per channel |

## 1. Conduction Losses (80 A burst)

With 6-step trapezoidal commutation and synchronous rectification, exactly two MOSFETs are in the current path at any instant: one in the PWM leg (high side or synchronous low side) and one static low side.

**Per-channel conduction loss:**
$$P_{cond,ch} = I_{ph}^2\,\big[2R_{ds}(T_j) + R_{pcb}\big]$$

**Temperature dependence (T_j = 100 °C):**
$$R_{ds}(100) = 1.2\,(1+0.006\cdot75) = 1.74\ \text{m}\Omega$$

**Numbers:**
- FET conduction: P = 6400 × 3.48 mΩ = **22.3 W**
- Copper loss: 6400 × 0.5 mΩ = **3.2 W**
- **P_cond,ch ≈ 25.5 W**

**Per-FET loss.** Each FET conducts for about 1/3 of the electrical period. Its instantaneous dissipation is 80² × 1.74 mΩ = **11.1 W**, and its period average is 22.3/6 ≈ **3.7 W**.

At burst eRPM (>1 kHz electrical), the electrical period (<1 ms) is short compared with the junction-to-board thermal time constant (~5–20 ms). The average value therefore governs the board rise. Junction ripple adds about +3–5 K.

**Thermal runaway check.** Positive feedback through α is stable if:
$$\frac{\partial P}{\partial T}\,R_{th} = P_{cond}\,\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha\Delta T}\,R_{th,ja} < 1$$

For 3.7 W per FET with R_th,ja,eff ≈ 4.2 K/W, the loop gain is about 0.064. The design is stable at the device level. The real risk is board-level heat accumulation (Section 3).

---

## 2. Switching Losses at 48 kHz

Only the PWM leg hard-switches. The high side switches against the low-side body diode.

| Term | Equation | Value |
|---|---|---|
| V-I overlap | ½·V·I·(t_r+t_f)·f_sw = 0.5×25.2×80×40n×48k | **1.94 W** |
| Reverse recovery | Q_rr·V·f_sw = 40n×25.2×48k | 0.05 W |
| Output capacitance | ½·C_o(er)·V²·f_sw = 0.5×1.5n×635×48k | 0.02 W |
| Dead-time diode conduction | 2·V_f·I·t_dead·f_sw = 2×0.8×80×100n×48k | **0.61 W** |
| Gate charge (2 switching FETs, mostly in driver) | 2·Q_g·V_gs·f_sw | 0.05 W |
| **P_sw,ch** | | **≈ 2.67 W** |

**Design levers:**
- Dead-time loss is 23% of switching loss. Trimming t_dead from 100 to 50 ns saves about 0.3 W per channel, but only if the driver's shoot-through margin allows it.
- Moving from 48 to 24 kHz halves P_sw (about −1.3 W per channel). This costs higher current ripple and audible noise.

---

## 3. Board Thermal Model

**Total burst dissipation (all four channels at 80 A):**
$$P_{tot} = 4\,(25.5 + 2.67) \approx \mathbf{113\ W}$$

**Steady state is impossible.** Prop-wash convection is h ≈ 100 W/m²K. The area is 2×(0.0305)² ≈ 1.86×10⁻³ m², giving R_th,conv ≈ 5.4 K/W. A steady-state rise of about 610 K is not achievable, so the design is purely capacity-limited.

### Lumped heat capacity (30.5×30.5, 8-layer, 2 oz)

| Mass | Value | Heat capacity |
|---|---|---|
| FR-4 | 1.49 cm³ × 1.85 g/cm³ = 2.75 g, c = 1.1 J/g·K | 3.0 J/K |
| Copper | 8 × 70 µm × 50% fill × 9.3 cm² ≈ 2.3 g, c = 0.385 J/g·K | 0.9 J/K |
| 24 MOSFETs + capacitors + solder | | ~0.4 J/K |
| **C_board** | | **≈ 4.3 J/K** |

### Burst duration limit

The first-order RC model is:
$$T_b(t) = T_a + P\,R_{conv}\left(1-e^{-t/\tau}\right),\qquad \tau = R_{conv}C = 23\ \text{s}$$

For t ≪ τ this reduces to:
$$t_{burst} \approx \frac{C\,\Delta T_b}{P - \Delta T_b/R_{conv}}$$

The junction runs above the board by:
$$\Delta T_{jb} = P_{FET}\,(R_{th,jc} + R_{th,cb}) = 4.7\ \text{W} \times (1.2 + 3.0) \approx 20\ \text{K}$$
Here P_FET = 113 W / 24 ≈ 4.7 W, and R_th,cb assumes a via-array pad.

Taking T_a = 35 °C and T_j,max = 125 °C:
- Board limit = 125 − 20 = 105 °C, so ΔT_b = 70 K.
- t_burst ≈ 4.3×70 / (113 − 13) ≈ **3.0 s** (all four motors at 80 A).
- With the 10 K design margin I recommend (T_b ≤ 95 °C): **≈ 2.6 s**.
- Single motor at 80 A, others at 20 A: P ≈ 28 + 3×(~2.2) ≈ 35 W, giving t ≈ 11
